svg.title: Install the Satori MCP server in three steps
svg.desc: A 21-second loop. Left, an AI agent terminal; right, three numbered steps that light up in turn. Step 1, Ask your agent: the user types "install https://docs-v2.satori.ci/modes/mcp/setup.html"; the agent fetches the page, runs "claude mcp add --scope user satori -- npx -y github:satorici/satori-mcp" and the satori server shows as connected. Step 2, Get a recommended playbook: the agent calls satori recommend_playbook, which detects python/uv and proposes five checks (lint: ruff check, format: ruff format --check, types: pyrefly check, unit: pytest -q, security: pyspector scan); the user answers yes, the agent writes .satori-llm.yml, adds a Satori verification section to CLAUDE.md and runs run_local once as a baseline: 5 checks ran, 0 findings. Step 3, Every change is verified: the user asks "add a backup endpoint"; the agent writes src/api/backup.py and runs run_local again, which reports 1 new finding not in the baseline: HIGH, PY106, CWE-78, src/api/backup.py line 14, use of subprocess.run with shell=True is a command injection risk. The agent replaces the shell command with an argument list, re-runs the playbook and gets 5 checks ran, 0 new findings.

text.tspan: └ MCP server · Configure your agent · Claude Code
claude mcp add --scope user satori -- npx -y github:satorici/satori-mcp
└ Added stdio MCP server satori to user config
✗ 1 new finding · not in the baseline

g.text: Use of subprocess.run with shell=True is a command injection risk.

text.tspan: ● Done. POST /projects/{name}/backup is in, verified by Satori.

g.text: Paste the setup link. Your agent adds
the Satori MCP server by itself.
It detects your stack and proposes lint,
format, type, unit and security checks.
After each edit the agent re-runs it and
fixes what was not in the baseline.
